national_news.title: India’s Space Economy Projected to Reach $40–45 Billion in 7–8 Years
bullets: Union Minister of State for Space Dr. Jitendra Singh stated that India’s space economy, currently valued at around $9 billion, is expected to expand to $40–45 billion over the next 7 to 8 years.
The statement was made at the 'Space, Sovereignty and New Economy' media roundtable organized by the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi.

Key growth drivers highlighted include increased domestic and foreign investment, faster regulatory approvals, predictable market demand, and building globally competitive commercial space enterprises.

national_news.title: Space Economy Growth Trajectory Driven by Private Reforms and Downstream Services
bullets: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted that space sector opening (2019–2020) and bodies like IN-SPACe are enabling India's growth toward a $40–45 billion space economy.
The government emphasizes a use-case-based approach, acting as anchor customers through proof-of-concept projects to create predictable demand for private space firms.

Beyond satellite launches, economic value will increasingly stem from downstream services, geospatial applications, Earth observation, and space-based disaster management support provided to neighbors like Myanmar, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka.

national_news.title: Aadhaar Authentication Made Mandatory for PM CARES for Children Scheme
bullets: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment notified that Aadhaar authentication or proof of possession is now required to avail scholarship benefits under the PM CARES for Children Scheme.
The scheme provides financial assistance for continuing education from Class 1st to 12th for children who lost their parents or legal guardians to the COVID-19 pandemic.

No child will be denied assistance due to lack of Aadhaar; alternative identity verification methods such as birth certificates, passports, voter IDs, and biometric/OTP-based verification will be allowed.

national_news.title: Indian Media & Entertainment Sector Must Target Global Markets: JS MIB at CII BIG Picture Summit
bullets: Addressing the 13th CII BIG Picture Summit in Mumbai, Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB), Senthil Rajan, called on India's media and entertainment industry to focus on creating original Intellectual Property (IP) for global audiences.

Highlighted government efforts to streamline film permissions through single-window mechanisms and the operationalization of the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) at a temporary campus in Mumbai.

Emphasized skill development and capacity building in emerging technologies including Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, Comics (AVGC), Virtual Reality (VR), Extended Reality (XR), and Artificial Intelligence (AI).
